questions.question: List six features of the combined school desk and explain the purpose of each in terms of design considerations.
questions.expected_answer: Steel tube frame: a light, strong frame structure that is cheap to weld, a cost and function choice. Sloping laminated top: easier to write on and read from, ergonomics, and the laminate resists ink and spills and wipes clean, durability and hygiene. Shelf under the top: stores books so the surface stays clear, function. Seat and backrest fixed to the frame: one stable unit that cannot be separated or stolen piece by piece, stability and cost. Plastic feet: protect the floor and reduce noise, impact on the room. Rounded corners with no sharp edges: safety for children.

questions.question: Write a design brief with four specifications and two constraints for a portable battery radio for users without reliable electricity.
questions.expected_answer: Brief: People in homes without reliable electricity need affordable access to news, music and information. Design a portable battery-powered FM and AM radio for general use that is simple to operate without instructions, robust enough for daily use, light enough to carry, and low in price. Specifications: runs at least fifty hours on one set of cells; weighs under 500 grams; has a telescopic aerial, tuning dial, volume control, band switch, headphone socket and carrying strap; survives a one metre drop. Constraints: moulded plastic case and standard electronic parts available in bulk; retail price below a set low amount.

questions.question: Explain why analysing existing designs is part of the investigate step and describe the four moves of a good analysis.
questions.expected_answer: Before designing something new a designer studies what already exists to learn what works, what fails and what users expect, which informs the brief and avoids repeating mistakes; this is investigation. The four moves: list the features as observations without judging; explain the purpose of each feature in terms of users, purpose, function, cost, safety, ergonomics, aesthetics and impact; evaluate by naming strengths and weaknesses with reasons; and reconstruct the brief, specifications and constraints the designer must have worked from.
